SELECTED_INDEX: 4
CONFIDENCE: 0.46
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows a very strong C=O stretching band at 1786 cm⁻¹ – characteristic of an acid-chloride carbonyl (expected 1790–1820 cm⁻¹), which is absent from all candidates except the acid-chloride methyl chloroformate (4).  
Supporting bands for 4:  
• 821 and 788 cm⁻¹ – strong C–Cl stretches of aliphatic chlorides.  
• 1007, 948 and 919 cm⁻¹ – C–O and C–Cl coupled stretches of the ‑O-CH₃ and ‑COCl group.  
• 1458 cm⁻¹ – CH₃ deformation; 2972 / 2854 cm⁻¹ – CH₃ ν(C–H) stretches.  
• 1156 and 1214 cm⁻¹ – C–O-CH₃ stretching modes expected for an alkoxy carbonyl chloride.  
No nitrile band (~2250 cm⁻¹, rules GFQ-003/004) is present, excluding candidate 10, and no Si–F (~1030 cm⁻¹, rule GFQ-040) band pattern excludes candidate 3. The absence of P=O (~1250 cm⁻¹) or C=S (~1050 cm⁻¹) bands eliminates candidates 1, 5, 8, 9. The observed high-frequency carbonyl band is too high for ordinary esters (candidates 2, 6). Thus the peak pattern best matches methyl chloroformate.
